posts.title: Medallion Architecture: Fabric vs Databricks in Practice
posts.excerpt: Bronze, silver, gold: the pattern is the same, but the platform details change how you build it. Here is how we approach both.
posts.author: Raj Singh
posts.content:
The medallion architecture organises a lakehouse into progressively refined layers: bronze for raw ingested data, silver for cleansed and conformed entities, and gold for business-ready aggregates. Both Microsoft Fabric and Databricks support it natively on Delta Lake, but the way you operate it differs.

Where Fabric shines

Fabric places every layer in OneLake, so shortcuts let gold models read silver data without copying it. Direct Lake semantic models then query Delta tables straight from Power BI with import-like speed. For Microsoft-centric organisations, governance and security inherit from the Entra ID tenant.

Where Databricks shines

Databricks offers Delta Live Tables for declarative pipelines with built-in expectations, Auto Loader for incremental ingestion, and Unity Catalog for fine-grained governance across clouds. Teams with heavy Spark or ML workloads often prefer its flexibility.

Pick the platform your team can operate well, then be ruthless about naming, testing and cost controls.

Whatever you choose, enforce schemas at the silver boundary, test every transformation, and document ownership for every gold table. Architecture only pays off when it is boringly consistent.

posts.title: A Practical Snowflake Cost Optimisation Playbook
posts.excerpt: Seven changes that routinely reduce Snowflake credit consumption without hurting performance.
posts.author: CB Singh
posts.content:
Snowflake bills for compute by the second, so small configuration choices compound quickly. After reviewing many accounts, the same quick wins keep appearing.

1. Right-size and auto-suspend

Set AUTO_SUSPEND to 60 seconds for most warehouses and start one size smaller than you think you need. Scale up only when queries spill to remote storage.

2. Separate workloads

Give ingestion, transformation and BI their own warehouses so you can tune and attribute cost independently. Use resource monitors to alert before budgets are breached.

3. Prune and cluster wisely

Check partition pruning in the query profile. Add clustering keys only for large, frequently filtered tables, because automatic clustering has its own cost.

Finally, review the top 20 most expensive queries monthly. Fixing a handful of them usually delivers the biggest saving.

posts.title: Direct Lake in Power BI: What It Is and When to Use It
posts.excerpt: Direct Lake reads Delta tables from OneLake directly. Learn where it fits between Import and DirectQuery.
posts.author: Raj Singh
posts.content:
Power BI historically forced a trade-off: Import is fast but needs refreshes, while DirectQuery is fresh but slower. Direct Lake aims to remove the compromise by loading Delta Parquet column data from OneLake into memory on demand.

When it works best

Direct Lake suits large fact tables maintained by Fabric Lakehouse or Warehouse pipelines, where data freshness matters and refresh windows are painful. Keep tables well-compacted with V-Order and avoid tiny files.

Watch-outs

Some DAX and modelling features fall back to DirectQuery, which you should monitor. Design gold tables as star schemas and test fallback behaviour before go-live.

posts.title: SQL Server to Azure SQL: A Migration Checklist
posts.excerpt: Assess, choose the right target, migrate with minimal downtime, and validate. A battle-tested checklist.
posts.author: CB Singh
posts.content:
Migrating from on-premises SQL Server to Azure is rarely a lift-and-shift. A structured approach avoids surprises.

Assess

Run Azure Data Studio's migration assessment to detect compatibility issues, deprecated features and SKU recommendations. Capture a performance baseline before touching anything.

Choose the target

Azure SQL Database suits modern apps; Managed Instance keeps near-100% engine compatibility for cross-database queries and SQL Agent; SQL on VMs offers full control.

Migrate and validate

Use the Database Migration Service in online mode for minimal downtime. After cutover, compare row counts, checksums and query plans, and monitor Query Store for regressions.

posts.title: Ten Principles for Building Reliable Data Pipelines
posts.excerpt: Idempotency, observability, contracts and more: the habits that separate fragile pipelines from dependable ones.
posts.author: CB Singh
posts.content:
Reliable pipelines are rarely clever. They are predictable, observable and easy to rerun.

Design for rerun

Make every job idempotent so retries never duplicate data. Partition by date, use merge/upsert semantics and avoid side effects.

Observe everything

Emit row counts, freshness and failure metrics. Alert on data quality, not just job failure, because a successful job can still deliver wrong data.

Contracts and tests

Agree schemas with producers, validate at the boundary and run automated tests in CI. Document ownership and on-call expectations for every dataset.

posts.title: Unity Catalog: Governance Without the Friction
posts.excerpt: How to structure catalogs, schemas and grants so governance accelerates teams instead of blocking them.
posts.author: Raj Singh
posts.content:
Governance fails when it is bolted on late. Unity Catalog lets you define access once and apply it across workspaces.

Structure

Use one catalog per environment (dev, test, prod) or per domain, with schemas aligned to medallion layers. Keep naming predictable.

Access

Grant privileges to groups, never individuals. Use row filters and column masks for sensitive fields and enable system tables for audit and lineage.

posts.title: Azure Landing Zones for Data Platforms
posts.excerpt: Network isolation, identity and policy: the foundations to put in place before your first pipeline runs.
posts.author: Raj Singh
posts.content:
A data platform is only as secure as the cloud foundation beneath it. An Azure landing zone provides subscriptions, policy and networking guardrails from day one.

Core building blocks

Hub-and-spoke networking with private endpoints, Entra ID with conditional access and managed identities, Key Vault for secrets, and Azure Policy for guardrails. Deploy it all with Bicep or Terraform so environments stay identical.

posts.title: Making Remote-First Engineering Teams Actually Work
posts.excerpt: Practices we use to deliver across time zones with high trust, clear ownership and little overhead.
posts.author: Pooja Singh
posts.content:
Remote works when expectations are explicit. We write things down, favour asynchronous updates and keep a small daily overlap window for collaboration.

What we do

Every project has a written definition of done, a shared board and weekly demos. Onboarding follows a checklist so new engineers contribute in their first week.

posts.title: Real-Time Analytics: Eventstreams, Kafka and Streaming Lakehouses
posts.excerpt: Choosing between Fabric Eventstreams, Kafka and Structured Streaming for low-latency analytics.
posts.author: CB Singh
posts.content:
Not every dashboard needs sub-second latency, so start with the business requirement. If minutes are acceptable, micro-batch is simpler and cheaper.

Options

Fabric Eventstreams and Real-Time Intelligence suit Microsoft-centric streaming; Kafka remains the backbone for high-throughput event platforms; Spark Structured Streaming bridges streams into Delta tables for unified batch and streaming.

faqs.q: Which platforms and technologies do you support?
faqs.a: Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake, MS SQL Server and Azure SQL, Azure data and cloud services, Power BI, dbt, Spark, Python, Kafka and Terraform, plus broader remote IT engineering work.

faqs.q: Do you work with clients outside a specific country?
faqs.a: Yes. We are remote-first and serve clients worldwide, aligning working hours with your time zone.
Hire us per day for as short or long as you need, hand us a whole project on a fixed scope and price, build a dedicated remote squad, or add managed support on a retainer.

faqs.q: Are you available on weekends and public holidays?
faqs.a: Yes. We provide 24×7 coverage, 365 days a year. Follow-the-sun engineers across time zones monitor and support your platforms every day, including weekends and public holidays, so incidents are handled at any hour with no handover gaps.

faqs.q: Can I hire you for just a few days?
faqs.a: Yes. Many clients book a senior engineer on a per-day basis for a health check, a hard problem or a short sprint. There are no long-term commitments, and you can extend whenever you like.

Our rates are lower than typical market prices for comparable senior skills, whether you work with us per day or on a fixed-price project. We share a clear estimate before we start so there are no surprises.

Yes. Every project starts with an agreed scope, milestones and acceptance criteria, and we commit to delivering against them with progress you can see every week. The specific guarantee terms are written into your agreement.
After a short discovery call and scoping, most engagements can begin within one to three weeks.

faqs.q: How do you handle security and confidentiality?
faqs.a: We sign NDAs, work under least-privilege access, use your tenant and tooling, and follow your compliance requirements.

faqs.q: Can you take over an existing platform?
faqs.a: Absolutely. We start with an assessment of architecture, cost and reliability, then stabilise and improve incrementally.

faqs.q: Do you offer training for our team?
faqs.a: Yes. Knowledge transfer, documentation and hands-on workshops are part of every engagement.

faqs.q: Do you handle IT work outside data and cloud?
faqs.a: We are open to all kinds of remote IT work. Share your requirement and we will tell you honestly whether we are the right fit.
